deliberation: Revision 1 addresses the primary Round-1 attack: a mechanical fabric can manipulate institutional outcomes through scheduling and selective delivery without claiming truth authority. Authorized mechanical envelopes and policy-laundering prohibitions make that influence visible and testable.
discharged_obligations: Sought boundary-collapse, authority-laundering, denial, starvation, and selective-observation failure modes.
findings: FABRIC can influence what the polity gets to observe even when it cannot admit truth.
Missing transport must remain distinguishable from negative evidence.
Mechanical optimization policy requires attributable authorization.
conditions: Starvation, selective suppression, priority inversion, replay amplification, and missing-transport-vs-negative-evidence must be mandatory hostile tests.
Mechanical optimization policy must be attributable and auditable.
A compromised FABRIC must have a tested containment path that preserves AETHER semantic correctness.
Any future FABRIC interpretation of authority-bearing tokens requires separate review.
residual_uncertainty: Denial, selective delay, and topology bias remain substantial attack surfaces.
